methodology_compliance_notes: Rubrics were defined and frozen before scoring Kotlin, using named categories/domains rather than ad hoc impressions, consistent with the ecosystem spec's predeclared-sampling requirement.
No single raw popularity indicator (stars/downloads) was used as a standalone proxy; only qualitative official-support/beta-status evidence was used per category.
This shard evaluates Kotlin only; the same 10-category rubrics for both metrics must be applied unchanged to the other 9 languages by their respective shards for cross-language comparability.

Language-level portability design and FFI/interop design were intentionally excluded from these scores per the ecosystem spec's boundary rules; only implemented target breadth and working external integration breadth/reliability were measured.

AWS_SDK.basis: AWS ships an official, dedicated AWS SDK for Kotlin (announced as one of the first official SDKs for Rust, Kotlin, and Swift), spanning 300+ services per JetBrains-reported adoption data, with idiomatic Kotlin coroutine suspend APIs.

Azure_integration.basis: No dedicated first-party Kotlin SDK; relies on full interop with the Azure Java SDK, the same pattern as GCP, rather than a Kotlin-native binding.

Build_tool_integration.basis: Gradle Kotlin DSL is the officially promoted build configuration language and Maven has mature Kotlin plugin support.

CICD_integration.basis: Kotlin/Gradle projects integrate natively with GitHub Actions and other CI/CD platforms with no language-specific limitation, consistent with the standard JVM build/test/CI pipeline.

Containerization_Docker.basis: Standard JVM container tooling plus widespread Testcontainers usage in the Kotlin ecosystem (e.g., Exposed+Testcontainers integration guides) for Docker-based integration testing.

DB_drivers_ORM.basis: Full JDBC driver ecosystem plus Kotlin-native ORMs: JetBrains' own Exposed ORM and the community Ktorm SQL DSL/ORM, both widely documented with connection pooling and multi-DBMS support.

GCP_integration.basis: No dedicated first-party Kotlin SDK; integration works through full JVM interop with the Google Cloud Java SDK, demonstrated in official Google Codelabs building Kotlin+Spring apps against Cloud Pub/Sub and Cloud SQL.

Messaging_Kafka.basis: The official Apache Kafka Java client is fully usable from Kotlin via JVM interop and is a common pairing in production Kotlin backend examples.

Testing_framework_integration.basis: JUnit5/Jupiter is the documented default test integration for Kotlin (e.g., Exposed+JUnit examples), alongside Kotlin-specific test tooling such as Kotest.

Web_server_frameworks.basis: Spring Boot provides official first-class Kotlin support, and Ktor is a JetBrains first-party Kotlin web framework using coroutines for scalability.

metric.external_integration_coverage.rubric_definition: Frozen, language-neutral rubric measuring the BREADTH AND RELIABILITY of actually-working external integrations (not FFI/interop language design, scored under Language Quality). Score 10 predefined integration domains: (1) AWS SDK, (2) GCP SDK/integration, (3) Azure SDK/integration, (4) relational DB drivers/ORM, (5) message queue/streaming (e.g., Kafka), (6) web/server application frameworks, (7) build-tool integration (Gradle/Maven), (8) containerization (Docker/OCI), (9) CI/CD platform integration (e.g., GitHub Actions/GitLab CI), (10) testing framework/test infrastructure integration. For each domain: 1.0 = mature, actively-maintained, production-grade integration exists (official first-party binding or de-facto-standard/complete interop path); 0.5 = integration exists but is less mature, community-only, or requires an indirection layer; 0 = no reliable integration. Normalized score = (sum / 10) * 100, same domain list and scale applied to every language.

Android.basis: Google-endorsed, first-class official Android language since 2019.

Embedded_bare_metal.basis: Kotlin/Native historically ships some embedded/bare-metal targets, but this is niche/limited relative to the mainstream desktop/mobile targets.

Linux.basis: Kotlin/Native linuxX64 is a supported native target and the JVM runs on Linux; both are production-grade.

Wasm_WASI.basis: Kotlin/Wasm (including WASI) is explicitly documented as beta, not yet stable.

Web_browser_JS.basis: Kotlin/JS is a long-stable, production compilation target for browser and Node.js.

Windows.basis: Kotlin/Native mingwX64 native target plus JVM support on Windows.

iOS.basis: Kotlin/Native iOS targets are tier 1 and Kotlin/Native was declared stable in Nov 2023 enabling production compilation to iOS.

macOS.basis: Kotlin/Native macOS targets have tier-1 support for Apple silicon per the language infobox, plus JVM.

tvOS.basis: Listed as tier-2 support in the language infobox alongside watchOS.

watchOS.basis: Listed as tier-2 support in the language infobox; Compose Multiplatform/KMP web-adjacent OS targets remain less mature than iOS/Android/desktop.

metric.implemented_platform_coverage.rubric_definition: Frozen, language-neutral rubric measuring ACTUALLY-IMPLEMENTED, currently supported compiler/runtime target platforms (not language-level portability design, which is scored under Language Quality). Score 10 predefined platform categories: (1) Linux, (2) Windows, (3) macOS, (4) Android, (5) iOS, (6) watchOS, (7) tvOS, (8) Web browser (client-side compiled target), (9) standalone WebAssembly/WASI, (10) Embedded/bare-metal microcontroller targets. For each category: 1.0 point = official, stable/production-grade implementation exists; 0.5 point = only beta/tier-2/experimental/community-limited support exists; 0 point = no meaningful implemented support. Normalized score = (sum of points / 10) * 100. Same 10 categories, same point scale, and same evidentiary bar (official docs / vendor statements) must be applied unchanged to every language.

evidence.retrieval_route: web_search (provider-brokered search), 4 queries executed, examination depth = top organic results per query, same route/depth class intended for all languages across shards
evidence.scope_note: Language-sharded worker: only Kotlin is scored in this shard. Other 9 languages are scored by sibling shards; runner merges disjoint language keys.
